case: registering a primitive with no predicate child, used in a value position
why: The benign twin of r19-allowlist-widened-in-json, differing in exactly the thing the refusal is about. `identity_value` is registered with one argument, `value`, typed JsonValue and classified `value` by `argument_positions` -- NO boolean child, so nothing about it can widen what satisfies a pin -- it is USED, in the value slot of guard.acceptance.resolution_reason_present's `nonempty` conjunct, and the digest is re-pinned by hand in the same edit because `argument_positions` moved. Nothing is added to `#/admissible_ancestors`, because nothing needs to be. This must PASS, and a checker that refused it would be refusing the registration of primitives rather than the widening of the allowlist -- a suite that rejects everything passes every adverse row, which is the pairing rule this fixture exists for. It also exercises the two controls the adverse case trips, in the direction that must not fire: the allowlist equality check (the JSON block still equals ADMISSIBLE_LITERAL) and the demanding-declaration check (no demanding role, so no entry required). RE-PINNED 2026-09-15 against the current registries. THE OLD DIGEST was `2d3cfe8ff2baf6e19188115a8444b94c78e8dd93ee48b17a2d6d047e3a4aad23`, computed over a primitive-registry.json of 57 primitives plus this fixture's `identity_value`; R44 then added the instant-offset primitive, so the tree as this fixture mutates it now holds 59 and the re-pin check (RC4-01) rejected the benign case with a digest mismatch rather than with anything about the allowlist. That was a false exclusion and RC4-01 was right: the digest is maintained BY HAND precisely so any movement in any argument position of any primitive stops the build until someone writes the new value, and a fixture that carries its own re-pin is not exempt from that. The new value `6fcac9724d2c25339bb2f1f12cefa9444e55c8a9ae715b23aacfafb54120014c` is what the command in `pinned-conjuncts.json#/argument_positions_digest_why` prints over the tree AS THIS FIXTURE MUTATES IT -- the committed registry with `identity_value` added, nothing frozen and no other primitive touched. The case is unchanged: the patch still widens the allowlist in JSON by registering a primitive and using it in a value position, and still re-pins in the same edit, which is exactly what makes it the benign twin of r19-allowlist-widened-in-json rather than a second copy of it.

value.semantics: Return the decoded current-authorized value unchanged; a naming wrapper for a value position, with no predicate child, no mutation and no new authority.
value.failure: unresolved on absent, ambiguous, stale, unauthorized or invalid input; never silently coerced to true or a guessed world fact
